title: Nottingham Forest’s Murillo out of Sunderland game, doubt for Europa League semi-final first leg
content:
Nottingham Forest defender Murillo will not be fit to face Sunderland on Friday and is also likely to miss at least the first leg of the Europa League semi-final against Aston Villa.

The Brazilian has a muscle problem that will leave him sidelined for the Premier League clash tomorrow night, as Forest look to extend their unbeaten run to eight games.

Vitor Pereira says the central defender will play again this season, but also that Murillo remains a doubt for next week.

“He is out. We will see. It is a muscle injury. I’m not a doctor, I cannot predict, but he will be out tomorrow,” said Pereira in his pre-match press conference.

“I think it will be more than one game. Yes (he will play again this season).”

If Forest can secure victory against the Premier League’s surprise package tomorrow, it will increase the gap between themselves and Tottenham Hotspur — who occupy the final relegation spot, to eight points — before they play at Wolves on Saturday.

Forest will also be without Callum Hudson-Odoi, with the winger having undergone surgery to repair a quadriceps injury on Tuesday.

“He is okay after the surgery. He is an important player for us, but the most important is for him to fully recover and come back at the level he used to have,” said Pereira of Hudson-Odoi, who is expected to return to full training in pre-season.

Fellow Brazilian Jair Cunha is the most likely replacement for Murillo in Sunderland, although Pereira could also call upon Morato or Zach Abbott.
